title: The Kindly Choir
premise: Orsen Galloway hosts a small-town overnight radio show, and for seven years the dead have been calling in—voices he's convinced are pranks, interference, or his own unraveling mind. When an excavation crew at the old Harrow farm unearths a cellar door sealed from the inside, the calls stop being deniable: they name Orsen, they recite things only he knows, and they ask him to give back what was taken in 1974. Digging into the town's buried history, Orsen learns that eleven people vanished that winter and the town chose silence over justice, feeding something beneath the frost to keep itself safe. To end it, Orsen must broadcast the truth the town has paid to suppress—and then walk through the door himself, offering what was taken, before the frost finishes writing its final pattern across everyone who stayed quiet.
about_author: Lior Thackeray is the pen name of a former late-night radio producer who spent a decade in stations where the equipment never quite behaved. They write horror about small communities and the bargains they make with the dark.

chapters.title: Dead Air
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. During a routine overnight broadcast, a caller describes her own funeral from last Tuesday; Orsen logs it as a prank like all the others. The emotional beat is weary denial—he's built careful systems of explanation, and we feel how much effort it takes to keep them standing.

chapters.title: The Door Sealed From Inside
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. The excavation crew at the derelict Harrow farm unearths a cellar door bolted shut from within, and the foreman asks Orsen on air if the town remembers what happened there in '74. That night, three dead callers speak in unison. Beat: denial cracks into dread.

chapters.title: What the Town Agreed Not to Say
chapters.summary: POV Orsen, with flashbacks to his arrival seven years ago. He searches the newspaper archive and finds eleven obituaries from winter 1974, all cut short, all missing from the bound volumes. An elderly listener warns him off air: some debts keep a town warm. Beat: isolation deepens.

chapters.title: Frost Patterns
chapters.summary: POV Maren Voss, the excavation foreman. Frost forms on her windows in shapes like handwriting; her crew starts hearing the radio play in empty trucks. She confronts Orsen, demanding answers he doesn't have. Beat: the horror spreads beyond Orsen, and guilt becomes contagious.

chapters.title: The Kindly Choir
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. The dead callers begin singing together during his show—a low, patient harmony that listeners phone in to praise. Orsen realizes the voices aren't accusing him; they're rehearsing something. Beat: terrible beauty; he stops wanting it to stop.

chapters.title: Nineteen Seventy-Four
chapters.summary: POV Edith Harrow via recovered cassette tapes. The recordings reveal the town's bargain: eleven outsiders and troublemakers were given to whatever lived beneath the frost, and every family since has inherited the debt. Beat: justice outside the law revealed as atrocity dressed up as survival.

chapters.title: Everyone Who Stayed Quiet
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. The town council offers him money and a transfer, revealing they've always known what the calls were. When he refuses, the frost reaches his studio windows mid-broadcast. Beat: staying invisible was never an option; complicity has a price tag and it's due.

chapters.title: Interference
chapters.summary: POV Maren. The choir takes Maren's missing crew members one by one, each disappearance punctuated by a call to Orsen's show from the taken. Maren and Orsen join forces, racing to open the sealed door before the final frost pattern completes. Beat: desperate alliance, rising panic.

chapters.title: The Final Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. On air, Orsen reads the names of the eleven and confesses the town's crime to every listening household, breaking the seal of silence. The choir swells; the door unbolts itself; the frost pattern completes into a doorway of its own. Beat: climax—truth as both weapon and key.

chapters.title: Give Back What Was Taken
chapters.summary: POV Orsen, closing with Maren. Orsen walks through the door carrying the confession, the tapes, and the town's shame, trading himself to settle a debt he didn't incur but benefited from. The calls cease; the station goes quiet. Maren keeps the frequency open, just in case. Beat: costly, ambiguous grace—the price of survival finally paid by someone.
